params.body:
## What was wrong

"Mijn aangeboden wagens" was one table in the order of the start date. With seventeen offers on screen it showed seventeen filled blue buttons, while five of those rows asked something of the dealer. The blue button changed meaning per row (bids, assign, borderel) and the row menu wrapped onto a second line under the buttons, so the action column was ragged and every row two lines tall. The state stood in three forms in one cell (a badge, a phrase, a date range), "Details" was a column holding only a toggle, the car name was a blue link, and at 1024px the action column ran out of its card.

## What it is now

- **The answer first.** One sentence above the list says what waits for the dealer and what still runs, counted over the whole list and not only the page.
- **One list, the state in front.** The first column is the state as one word (to assign, to release, to pick up, running, documents, closed, done) with the time under it. Amber only where time runs out, red only where a pickup term has passed.
- **What has to happen first is on top** as long as the dealer did not sort: what waits for him with the term that runs out soonest first, then what runs, then documents-only vehicles, then what is finished. A sort the dealer picks orders the whole list across every state, as before, and stays his until he picks "what has to happen first" in the sort menu.
- **Every control in a column of its own**, so it stands in the same place on every row and the right edge is straight: two quiet actions, one filled button only where the dealer must act, the row menu. Nothing wraps.
- **The bids say their count on the row** ("Biedingen 4"); a zero is quiet and still tappable.
- **One row height**, the photo and its placeholder in one frame, the car name in ink, the bid right-aligned over its bidder. "Details" is no longer a column: a click on the row opens them as a quiet table.
- **Short dates.** A period reads "2 sep tot 9 sep" in the language of the reader: the year only when it is not the current year, once when both ends share it, on both ends when they differ (`App\Support\ShortDate`). The same writing in the period column, the details, the phone card and the date of a documents-only vehicle.
- **One markup for every width.** Between 960 and 1240px the quiet actions keep their place and drop their word (the tooltip says it). Below that the row is a card with the actions as one row under it; on a phone every target is 44px and the menu is a bottom sheet. Nothing scrolls sideways.

## Nothing that was one tap became two

| Kind of row | One tap before | One tap now |
|---|---|---|
| Bidding runs | Toon aan klant, Biedingen, details, open the car | the same, the bids with their count |
| To assign | Toon aan klant, Bod toewijzen, details, open the car | the same, plus Biedingen |
| Assigned (to release) | Toon aan klant, Vrijgeven, details, open the car | the same, plus Biedingen (was two taps) |
| Released (to pick up) | Toon aan klant, Afgehaald & beoordelen, details, open the car | the same, plus Biedingen (was two taps) |
| Done or closed | Toon aan klant, Biedingen, details, open the car | the same |
| Documents only | Overeenkomst, Borderel, open the car | the same, plus details |
| Two taps (row menu), any row | the documents of a bidding, copy, edit, delete | the same five |

This is rule B1-1.19 now, with a test (`OfferedCarsListTest`).

## How it is built

- `App\Support\OfferedCars` holds what an offer is (waiting for the dealer, running, documents only, finished) as one rule read twice: by the query, which counts and orders, and by the model, which says what a row shows. A test holds the two together for every kind of offer.
- `ExportVehicleRepository::getOfferedList` is the list; `getOfferedOfKind` counts for the answer.
- The old row and card partials are gone with their rules: `refresh.css` shrinks by 84 lines and the blade `onclick=` count by 19; the budgets in `tests/quality-ratchet.json` and one count in the PHPStan baseline are lowered to match. The new row has no inline `onclick`.
- Rules B1-1.14, B1-1.17, B1-5.13, B1-5.14 and B1-5.16 describe the new list; B1-1.19 is new.
- Strings in Dutch, French, English and German; the German follows the words already in use (Gebot, zuweisen, freigeben, Abholung, Auktion).

## Checked

- The full suite on a fresh local database: green on the final commit.
- PHPStan without errors, pint on the new files, `npm run build`, `bin/rules-sources` without problems.
- In a browser at 1440, 1024 and 390 with seventeen offers of every kind: each quiet action on one vertical line, a click on the row opens its details, "Toon aan klant" and "Overeenkomst" open their window, the row menu opens with its five items.
- At 1440: the bids link and the car name go to their page, and a chosen sort orders the whole list.

## Not checked

- Release for pickup, picked up and rate, copy and delete were not clicked in the browser, because they change data. Their routes and the way they are called are unchanged and covered by the existing tests.
- French, English and German were rendered in tests only for the dates; the screens were looked at in Dutch.
- The German strings were written against the existing vocabulary but not read by a German speaker. Spanish has no strings for this list.
- Real data: the list was looked at with a local demo dataset, not with a dealer who has hundreds of offers.

## Open

- The intro under the title says 14 days to assign; the platform counts 15 (R B1-3.6). Not touched here.
- A chosen sort stays until the dealer picks "what has to happen first" again. The list remembered the sort before as well.
params.title: My offered cars: one calm list that answers first and keeps every one-tap action
